newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police say six militants killed in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Indian police say six militants killed in Kashmir.

text.p: Six separatist guerrillas were killed in a gunbattle in India's northern state Jammu and Kashmir, a senior Indian police officer said on Thursday.

"Last evening six suspected foreign militants were killed in an encounter which lasted almost six hours with B.S.F. (Border Security Forces)," Gurbachan Jagat, Director General of Jammu and Kashmir police, told a news conference.
Indian authorities say Pakistan trains and arms foreign mercenaries and Kashmiri militants. Islamabad says it offers only political and diplomatic support to the separatists.
Nine separatist guerrillas were killed on Monday by Indian paramilitary troops in two different shootouts, police said.
The latest killings took place at Sangeenpora, a small hamlet on the outskirts of Anantnag town is 55 km (35 miles) south of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in insurgency related violence since 1990 in Jammu and Kashmir, India's only Moslem majority state.
